connectors.name: Google Drive
connectors.person: Document owner and last editor email
connectors.detail: The reference connector, shipping since launch. Each subfolder of the shared root becomes its own boundary with search and read tools, so restructuring, legal hold and team documents each map to a policy domain. Results carry the owner and last-editor email, which is what the policy counts as people. Read only unless you pass --allow-write, which adds a folder-fenced create tool governed as egress.

connectors.name: Slack
connectors.person: Message author (Slack user id, email when resolvable)
connectors.detail: Read is fenced per channel, so #legal or #finance becomes its own information barrier. Posting is a governed write, refused as egress after an assistant has read untrusted content. Every message carries its author, so people-count rules apply in Slack exactly as in HR records. A plain bot token is enough; no user search token is required.

connectors.name: GitHub
connectors.person: Issue, PR and commit author (login, email when exposed)
connectors.detail: Read is fenced per repository, so the security repo is its own boundary. Search covers issues and pull requests; read also fetches a file by path. Opening an issue is a governed write. Issues, PRs and commits carry their author, so the policy counts people across GitHub results.

connectors.name: Jira
connectors.person: Reporter and assignee email (account id fallback)
connectors.detail: Read is fenced per Jira project. Search runs JQL scoped to the project; read returns an issue with its description flattened from Atlassian Document Format. Creating an issue is a governed write. Each issue carries its reporter and assignee, by email where Atlassian privacy allows, and by account id otherwise, so the accumulator can always count people.

connectors.name: Salesforce
connectors.person: Record email and record owner email
connectors.detail: Read is fenced per Salesforce object. Search runs SOQL by name; every record exposes an identifiable person, the record email for Leads and Contacts and the record owner email otherwise, so a bulk export trips an entity_budget rule before it drains the CRM. Creating a record is a governed write.

connectors.name: Notion
connectors.person: Page creator and last editor email
connectors.detail: Read is fenced per Notion database. Search lists pages and filters by title; read flattens a page and its blocks to text. Creating a page is a governed write. Pages carry their creator and last editor, resolved to email when the integration has user information, so the policy counts people across Notion results.

roadmap.name: Confluence
roadmap.note: Atlassian wiki, spaces as boundaries; shares the Jira auth model.

roadmap.name: Microsoft 365
roadmap.note: SharePoint, Teams and Outlook over Microsoft Graph. Highest reach, heaviest auth.

roadmap.name: ServiceNow
roadmap.note: Incidents, changes and CMDB tables, each mapped to a domain.

roadmap.name: Box
roadmap.note: Files fenced per folder, like the Drive reference connector.

roadmap.name: Zendesk
roadmap.note: Support tickets fenced per group; requesters and agents count as people.
